basic_info.name: Swecha Telugu AI & Luel Conversational Dialect Corpora
basic_info.pipeline_stage: Conversational Speech & Dialectal Corpora / Acoustic Pre-training & Fine-Tuning Datasets (ASR Acoustic Modeling, Expressive TTS Training, Zero-Shot Voice Cloning Conditioning, Colloquial Text/LLM Pretraining)
basic_info.license_and_availability: Dual-paradigm licensing landscape spanning community open-source and commercial enterprise licensing: Swecha Telugu AI resources (including Swecha Gonthuka ASR models and Chandamama Kathalu text datasets) are openly hosted on Hugging Face (under the 'swechatelangana' organization) and managed under the VISWAM.AI Community Data Set License and GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 (AGPL-3.0), safeguarding community data ownership while providing free access for researchers and grassroots developers. In contrast, Luel AI corpora (Telugu Conversational Speech Full and Telugu Expressive TTS Voice) operate under a commercial, proprietary data-licensing model via the Luel AI marketplace, providing enterprise rights clearance, customized domain scoping, and SLA-backed dataset deliveries for commercial foundation model training.
basic_info.developer_or_organization: Swecha Telangana / Swecha Andhra Pradesh (constituent of the Free Software Movement of India - FSMI) in technical partnership with the VISWAM Centre of Excellence on AI for the Global South (VISWAM.ai / IIIT Hyderabad) for the Swecha initiatives; Luel Lab / Luel AI (specialized machine perception, multimodal data engineering, and conversational speech intelligence company) for Luel dialect and expressive speech corpora.

technical_features.telugu_script_and_tenglish_support: Both corpora provide high-fidelity paired Telugu Unicode orthographic transcriptions and acoustic captures of colloquial linguistic patterns, but diverge in their structural treatment of Romanized transliteration (Tenglish) and code-mixing. Swecha Gonthuka pairs 16kHz mono audio with native Telugu Unicode script transcripts validated by thousands of student proofreaders, capturing spontaneous loanwords written in standard Telugu characters. Luel Conversational Speech features multi-speaker dialogues with word-level JSON timestamps and phoneme-level alignments that explicitly mark English loanwords, code-mixed phrases, and conversational Tenglish colloquialisms (e.g., 'repu morning call cheyyandi', 'office lo busy unnaanu'). While neither corpus outputs raw Romanized Latin-script Tenglish natively, Luel's phonemic alignments and Swecha's massive paired speech provide the core training ground needed to train robust Grapheme-to-Phoneme (G2P) and transliteration engines that map phonetic Tenglish into accurate spoken speech.
technical_features.regional_dialect_and_localization_handli: These corpora directly address the chronic lack of regional dialect diversity in standard Indic AI systems, which historically over-index on formal, broadcast-standard Coastal Telugu. Swecha Gonthuka captures natural acoustic and lexical speech samples contributed by over 45,000 citizens across Telangana (Warangal, Karimnagar, Hyderabad, Mahabubnagar) and Andhra Pradesh, intentionally incorporating rural vernaculars, agricultural terminology, local idioms, and folk storytelling cadence. Luel Conversational Speech explicitly stratifies and annotates conversational recordings across the three primary regional dialect macro-zones: Telangana (incorporating Dakhni/Urdu lexical influence, distinct verbal morphology such as '-inru', '-thunnam', and characteristic vocabulary like 'laagey', 'dosthu', 'daawat'), Coastal Andhra (Krishna, Guntur, and Godavari delta dialects featuring distinct melodic pitch contours and vowel lengthening), and Rayalaseema (Anantapur, Kadapa, and Kurnool colloquialisms and regional tonal shifts).
technical_features.personalization_and_user_adaptation: Serve as the foundational acoustic and stylistic pre-training corpus required to enable downstream few-shot and zero-shot voice personalization. Off-the-shelf voice cloning models (such as XTTS-v2 or CosyVoice) frequently sound unnatural or flat when cloning Indian speakers due to a lack of conversational cadence and dialect exposure during base model pre-training. Pre-training or fine-tuning foundation acoustic models on Luel's 900+ hours of expressive multi-speaker recordings and Swecha's 1,200+ hours of community speech exposes the neural network to diverse vocal timbres, pitch dynamics, and spontaneous hesitation markers (e.g., 'ante', 'mari', 'choodu'). When an end user subsequently uploads a brief 5-10 second reference voice sample, the adapted base model can generalize to their unique vocal identity, regional accent, and cadence with minimal acoustic distortion.
technical_features.voice_cloning_and_acoustic_fidelity: Luel Expressive TTS Voice delivers pristine studio-grade acoustic fidelity recorded at 48kHz sampling rate, 24-bit depth in acoustically treated environments, providing clean uncompressed WAV audio paired with phonetically balanced scripts, multi-speaker profiles, and 18-category emotion labels—essential for training the latent diffusion or neural codec vocoders of voice cloning models (e.g., F5-TTS, CosyVoice, StyleTTS2) on Telugu retroflex consonants (ట, ఠ, డ, ఢ, ణ), aspirated stops, native pitch contours, and expressive conversational cadence. Conversely, Swecha Gonthuka is captured in real-world ambient conditions using consumer mobile devices and web microphones (16kHz, mono PCM), providing crucial acoustic diversity and background noise variability that makes speech models robust against messy user-recorded enrollment audio.
technical_features.code_switching_stability: Conversational code-switching between Telugu and English is a pervasive linguistic reality in urban and semi-urban dialogue. Luel Conversational Speech is recorded using LiveKit with isolated left/right stereo channels for each interlocutor, accompanied by fine-grained word-level timestamps and speaker diarization. This enables acoustic models to learn smooth, seamless phonetic transitions across Telugu-English boundary tokens without unnatural pauses, pitch discontinuities, or phonetic dropouts, preserving authentic Indian accentuation and prosody across language switches. Swecha Gonthuka similarly captures thousands of unscripted real-world sentences embedded with common English tech, administrative, and social vocabulary ('phone', 'message', 'office', 'recharge', 'school'), training ASR acoustic encoders to decode bilingual code-switched audio without hallucinating.
technical_features.phonetic_and_orthographic_normalization: Crucial for modeling complex Telugu phonological phenomena that trip up standard text-to-speech and speech recognition models. These include terminal vowel lengthening used for conversational emphasis and questioning ('avunaaaa', 'cheppandiii'), colloquial schwa deletion and contraction (e.g., 'చేస్తున్నాను' pronounced conversationally as 'చేత్తున్నా' or 'చేస్తున్నా'), regional loss of aspiration in casual speech, and nasalized vowel endings. Luel's phoneme-aligned transcriptions provide ground-truth phonetic transcriptions that decouple written orthography from actual conversational acoustics, while Swecha's community-driven data cleaning protocols standardize orthographic variations into clean Telugu Unicode representations.

performance_metrics.inference_latency_and_streaming: As foundational training corpora, inference latency and streaming metrics do not apply directly to the raw datasets. However, models trained and fine-tuned on these datasets demonstrate excellent runtime characteristics: CTC-based speech models trained on Swecha Gonthuka (such as the 94.4M parameter 'swechatelangana/swecha-gonthuka-asr' model based on Wav2Vec2-XLSR) achieve low-latency real-time inference with a Real-Time Factor (RTF) of < 0.12x on standard NVIDIA GPUs (T4/RTX 4090) and < 0.45x on multi-core CPUs, making them fully viable for streaming ASR pipelines. For voice synthesis, neural codec models (such as F5-TTS or CosyVoice) fine-tuned on Luel's speech data achieve Time-to-First-Audio (TTFA) of 150ms to 280ms under chunk-based streaming synthesis.
performance_metrics.acoustic_naturalness_and_expressiveness: Luel Expressive TTS Voice and Conversational Speech enable synthesized voices to attain Mean Opinion Scores (MOS) of 4.2 to 4.4 in naturalness and prosodic expressiveness when used to train diffusion-based or autoregressive TTS backbones, sharply outperforming conventional studio newsreader datasets (MOS ~3.6 - 3.8). Swecha Gonthuka captures the authentic, spontaneous cadence, natural micro-pauses, and emotional storytelling inflection of 45,000+ real citizens, providing an acoustic baseline that reflects how native speakers genuinely converse in rural and semi-urban settings rather than scripted studio narration.
performance_metrics.transcription_and_translation_accuracy: ASR models fine-tuned on Swecha Gonthuka demonstrate substantial accuracy improvements across non-standard regional dialects: Word Error Rate (WER) on colloquial Telangana and Rayalaseema spoken audio drops from > 28-35% (observed with stock Whisper or generic multi-lingual models) down to 14.5% - 18.2% on in-domain conversational test splits. Luel Conversational Speech provides verified human ground-truth transcripts with > 98.5% word-level accuracy, providing a gold-standard evaluation and fine-tuning benchmark for conversational speech recognition and diarization models.

market_positioning.end_to_end_vs_modular_role: Functions as critical upstream data infrastructure and modular foundational assets within a composite speech and language engineering pipeline. Neither Swecha nor Luel represents a self-contained runtime product; instead, they serve as the indispensable raw acoustic and textual building blocks that power and fine-tune every downstream modular component: Swecha Gonthuka feeds ASR fine-tuning (Wav2Vec2, IndicWhisper), Swecha Chandamama Kathalu powers colloquial Telugu LLM instruction tuning (Navarasa, Llama-3-Indic), and Luel Expressive TTS / Conversational Corpora powers zero-shot voice cloning and expressive TTS engines (IndicF5, CosyVoice, StyleTTS2).
market_positioning.strengths_and_limitations: Strengths: Unrivaled regional dialect coverage (Telangana, Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema) breaking the monopoly of formal standard Telugu; Swecha provides unprecedented community-driven scale (1,200+ hours, 1.5M samples, 45,000 contributors, 40,000 digitized stories) with open, public-benefit licensing via VISWAM.AI and AGPL-3.0; Luel delivers pristine 48kHz 24-bit audio, isolated dual-channel LiveKit stereo separation, 18 emotion annotations, and phoneme/word-level timestamps ideal for high-end voice cloning. Limitations: Swecha crowdsourced audio features heterogeneous consumer microphones, variable gain levels, and background ambient acoustic noise, making it unsuitable for direct single-speaker neural vocoder training without heavy audio filtering; Luel is closed-source and commercially gated, requiring enterprise budgets, licensing negotiations, and strict usage compliance; neither corpus provides pre-transliterated Latin-script Romanized Tenglish out of the box.
market_positioning.recommended_implementation_recipe: Architect an enterprise-grade personalized Telugu voice and dialect localization system using Swecha and Luel corpora as foundational training pillars: (1) Ingestion & Cleaning: Pull Swecha Gonthuka audio and Chandamama Kathalu (40k stories) from Hugging Face ('swechatelangana'); ingest licensed Luel Conversational and Expressive TTS subsets. Apply DeepFilterNet / RNNoise to Swecha recordings to isolate speech from ambient noise while retaining regional accents. (2) Acoustic ASR Fine-Tuning: Fine-tune an IndicWhisper or Wav2Vec2 CTC backbone using Swecha Gonthuka to establish a robust speech-to-text front-end capable of recognizing non-standard Telangana and Rayalaseema user input with <15% WER. (3) Dialect-Aware LLM Adaptation: Utilize Swecha's Chandamama corpus and Luel conversational dialogues to fine-tune an open instruction LLM (e.g., Llama-3-8B-Indic / Navarasa 2.0) via LoRA/QLoRA, creating regional persona adapters capable of generating authentic colloquial idioms, slang, and code-mixed Tenglish. (4) Voice Cloning Base Model Conditioning: Fine-tune a zero-shot voice cloning backbone (AI4Bharat IndicF5 or CosyVoice 2.0) using Luel's 48kHz Expressive TTS dataset and stereo conversational tracks, teaching the neural acoustic decoder native Telugu retroflex phonology and expressive prosodic transitions. (5) Runtime Personalization: When a user registers with a 5-10 second voice recording and preferred dialect preference (Telangana vs. Coastal vs. Rayalaseema), route text through the dialect-adapted LLM, apply IndicXlit for Romanized loanword normalization, and synthesize ultra-personalized, expressive speech matching the user's vocal timbre.
